t: the commandment of the red heifer. With whose ashes one who is impure from a corpse is purified (Numbers chapter 19).
and if she was old. Over four years.
lest she blacken and be disqualified. As below, halachah 2.
and they do not buy a heifer. They do not purchase it when it is younger than this age.
they fix a price for it, etc.. They set its price, but do not pay until it grows.

from the terumah of the chamber. The coins set aside in three boxes from the half-shekel funds placed in the chamber in the Temple (see Hilchot Shekalim 2:4), with which public offerings are purchased, including the red heifer (ibid. 4:1).
this is what is said in the Torah: perfect. That this does not mean free of blemish, since it is explicitly written of it "in which there is no blemish."
perfect in redness. That it be entirely red.
a dwarf was valid like other sacrificial animals. For a dwarf is disqualified in a person serving in the Temple but not in an animal (see Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash 8:14).
in a single hole. That grow together from one root in the skin.
cups. A cup is a cluster of adjacent hairs (like a curl).
and they prove each other. For although the hairs grow in separate cups, they are adjacent and aligned opposite each other.
their root. The place where the hairs grow.

and he is not concerned about shearing of sacred animals. For the law of the heifer is like that of consecrated property for Temple upkeep, for which the prohibition of shearing is rabbinic (see Hilchot Me'ilah 1:12), and in this case they permitted it.
and it must remain. After he cut off the black part of the hair.
so that it can be removed with tweezers. That it be long enough to be taken by scissors (R. Y. Kafah explained, based on Commentary on the Mishnah, Negaim 4:4, that it refers to tweezers).
it is as if it were not. If the reddish base is less than enough to be taken with tweezers, it is considered as if the hair were entirely black or white, and removing it does not help.
its hooves. The horny part that covers the ends of the toes.
he cuts off. He will cut off the black part.
a wart. A wart.

even though red hair grew in its place, it is invalid. Since it is not perfect in redness (see Raavad and commentators; and in Mishnah Achronah (Parah 2:2) and Aruch HaShulchan (53:22) they wrote that the disqualification is due to a blemish).
all the blemishes that disqualify sacrificial animals. From being offered on the altar (for the list of blemishes see Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash chapter 7 and Hilchot Issurei Mizbe'ach chapter 2).
one born by caesarean. An offspring taken out through the wall of the abdomen and not through the womb (a caesarean section).
mechir. That was exchanged for a dog (see Hilchot Issurei Mizbe'ach 4:16-18).
etnan. That was given to a prostitute as her pay (see ibid. halachot 8-15).
a treifah. An injured animal that is likely to die soon (for the definition of this term see Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 4:6-9).
that was mounted. A person had relations with it, and these things disqualify other sacrificial animals from being offered on the altar (see Hilchot Issurei Mizbe'ach 3:4, 3:6-7).
even though it is like consecrated property for Temple upkeep. For it is not offered on the altar, and consecrated property for Temple upkeep is not disqualified by these things.
since Scripture called it a sin offering. Scripture calls the heifer "a sin offering," and from this it is learned that for certain laws the heifer has the law of an offering (see also below 2:3).
for he does not damage his animal. Since mating might harm it (and the same is the law for other offerings, see Hilchot Issurei Mizbe'ach 3:15).
for work disqualifies it. If he used it for any work, it is disqualified.

and in the heifer whose neck is broken, etc.. When a slain person is found and it is not known who struck him, the city nearest the slain person is commanded to bring a heifer and break its neck (see Hilchot Rotzeach chapters 9-10). And from the verse "which has not been worked" it is learned that work disqualifies this heifer (ibid. 10:3-4).
he did other work as with a yoke. For it is written "which has not been worked."
he brought it in to thresh. To the place where grain is threshed.
he hung onto its tail and crossed the river with it. He used it for help in crossing the river.
he folded the rope over it. The rope with which he pulls the animal, and placed it on its back.
a covering of sacks. A sort of belt tied around an animal for carrying sacks and loads.
if it was rebellious. And he feared it might run away.
for any guarding that does not require a burden is a burden. Compare Hilchot Shabbat 20:8.
for another purpose it is invalid. Because of the yoke.
if by his will. The owner's will.
which has not been worked. From the passive form "worked" it is learned that even if the work was done by itself, it is disqualified as long as it was done by the owners' will.
therefore if a bird rested on it it is valid, etc.. For the owners have no benefit from this. But from a male animal they do have benefit, since it can become pregnant and give birth.
he brought it into a herd. A place where cattle are gathered, for example where they were there for threshing grain.
and it threshed by itself, it is valid. Since the threshing was not by his will.

he brought it in so that it would nurse and thresh. For example, if its mother was threshing and he brought the daughter there to nurse, and he also intended that she thresh (see also Hilchot Chovel U'Mazik 7:5).
a heifer in which a blemish was born. After they had consecrated it.
it is redeemed. They desacralize it into coins of its value and it goes out to ordinary status.

it is redeemed for its hide, etc.. Just as sacrificial animals of the altar are not redeemed so that their flesh may be fed to dogs (Hilchot Issurei Mizbe'ach 2:10), so the heifer is not redeemed for this purpose but only for the use of its hide.
and it does not atone. It is not fit for making sin offering ashes from it.
it was slaughtered on top of its pyre. In the place designated for it (see below 3:1-2).
it has no redemption ever. For it is a disgrace to take it out to ordinary status after they have treated it with all the procedures required in its slaughter.
it is redeemed without a blemish. Unlike sacrificial animals of the altar, which are redeemed only with a blemish.
and by oral tradition. The tradition of the Sages.
this one is done by Elazar. Who was the deputy of the high priest, but for all other heifers it makes no difference by which priest it is done.
four garments. The four garments of an ordinary priest (for their details see Hilchot Kelei HaMikdash 8:1).

who were tevul yom. Who became impure with a primary source of impurity and have already immersed but the evening has not yet come, and for certain matters they are still considered impure (Hilchot She'ar Avot HaTum'ot 10:1).
for their sun had not yet set. The evening after their immersion had not yet come.
pure for second tithe. For second tithe is eaten in purity and a tevul yom is valid for it (Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni 3:4).
the Sadducees. People who challenge the tradition and authority of the Sages of the Oral Torah (see Hilchot Teshuvah 3:8, Hilchot Mamrim 3:3).
with those whose sun had set. And not with tevulei yom.
by a creeping creature or the like. One of the primary sources of impurity.
all the vessels into which the ashes of the heifer are put. Which must be pure (below 13:1).
one who cuts a tube of cane. Empties the inside of the reed and makes it into a container vessel that can become impure.
he renders it impure and immerses it. In order to nullify the words of the Sadducees, as in the previous halachah.

it requires immersion because they treated it like one impure from a corpse, etc.. A rabbinic decree that a tube made for sin offering ashes is treated as impure from a corpse and renders impure the one who makes it and the one who immerses it.
like one impure from a corpse on his seventh day. After the sprinkling was done on him on the third and seventh and he requires only immersion (see below 11:1-2).

but he renders it impure in order to show the Sadducees. Although they treated it as impure from a corpse, since this is impurity only by rabbinic decree, it is no demonstration to the Sadducees, and he must render it impure again to nullify the words of the Sadducees.
valid with tevulei yom. Above 1:13-14.
just as they separate the high priest for the service of Yom Kippur. See Hilchot Avodat Yom HaKippurim 1:3.
and he is impure for seven days. Like anyone who has relations with a niddah (see Hilchot Metamei Mishkav U'Moshav 3:1-3).

the chamber in which he sat all seven days was the northeast one. It seems that this refers to the high priest's chamber, which was also called the Wood Chamber and the Parhedrin Chamber (see Hilchot Avodat Yom HaKippurim 1:3 and the commentary there).

to remind him that this is like a sin offering that is slaughtered in the north. For the red heifer is like an offering for several laws since Scripture called it a sin offering (see above 1:7), and a sin offering is slaughtered on the north side (Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 5:2-3).
even though it is slaughtered outside. Below 3:2.
sin offering water. Living water into which the ashes of a red heifer were put and which was properly prepared to purify one impure from a corpse (and its laws are explained below, chapters 6-10).
because it is impossible for him not to be on the third day of his impurity. For three days earlier he was already in the chamber in the Temple and could not have become impure.

and by law he would need sprinkling only on the third and seventh from the separation. For the law of one impure from a corpse is that sprinkling is done on him on the third day and the seventh day from when he became impure or from when he came to be purified (below 11:1-2; and compare Hilchot Avodat Yom HaKippurim 1:4).
on the fourth day of the week. On Wednesday.
for sprinkling does not override Shabbat. For this is like an act of repair, which is forbidden on Shabbat (Hilchot Shabbat 23:8, and see Hilchot Korban Pesach 6:6).
and the fourth does not need sprinkling. As explained in the previous halachah.

they sprinkle on him from the ashes of a heifer, a different heifer each day, from those that were already burned. Each day they sprinkle from the ashes of a different heifer from among those burned in the past (see below, end of chapter 3).
they sprinkle on him from it all six. All the days except the fourth day, as above halachah 4.
for the sprinkler must be pure. Below 13:1.
and likewise the vessels with which they fill and sanctify. The vessels in which they draw the living water and put the ashes of the heifer into it.
built on the rock. A natural rock under which it is unlikely that a corpse was buried.

underneath them is hollow. That beneath the courtyards there is a hollow space of at least a handbreadth in height, so that even if a corpse is buried under the rock after all, its impurity does not break through and rise to the sky but is stopped in the hollow air (see Hilchot Tum'at Met 7:5).
a grave of the deep. This is what a grave is called that is not known to anyone at all.

they bring bulls because their bellies are swollen. So that the children's feet will not hang in the air and there will be no concern that they overshadow a corpse on the way (Commentary on the Mishnah, Parah 3:2).
and they place doors on their backs, etc.. And the doors create a tent that separates between the children and impurity that may be beneath them.
